response.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(CAST(l.DNA AS REAL)) AS avg_anti_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` > 180 GROUP BY p.SEX;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN to Patient drops lab records with no matching patient ID, as the request specifies.
GROUP BY p.SEX keeps each recorded SEX value as its own group. NULL and empty-string SEX values form separate groups, and both are kept.

Laboratory.DNA is TEXT. The query casts it to REAL, so NULL or blank values are skipped. Non-numeric text such as '<8' or '+' becomes 0 in SQLite and would pull the average down. The actual contents of DNA are not in the context, so this is unverified.

AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) computes the difference per lab record. A record with a NULL ALB or TP yields a NULL difference and is ignored. An average over zero non-NULL values returns NULL, which displays as empty. No ROUND is applied.
Each qualifying lab record counts once. Patients with several qualifying records contribute each record, not one averaged value per patient.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat only numeric-looking DNA text as a value, so non-numeric entries are excluded from the anti-DNA average instead of being cast to 0.
alternatives.sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(CASE WHEN l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l.DNA) <> '' AND l.DNA NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.]*' THEN CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) END) AS avg_anti_dna, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` > 180 GROUP BY p.SEX;
